Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split that between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

From 6 April 2027, investors under 65 will be capped at £12,000 a year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027, and you must be 18 or over. You can split the £20,000 between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

Changes announced from 6 April 2027 include a £12,000 cash ISA cap for investors under 65. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Sorry about that. Here is a corrected answer using only what the earlier search returned.

The ISA guide says adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year. It also says a Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. It does not say whether someone under 18 can open an ISA with us, so I can't confirm that for your daughter. Please raise it with your adviser.

The source is the ISAs guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

You must be aged 18 to 39 to open one. Withdrawals not covered by the exceptions incur a 25% government charge. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Per the guide, a Lifetime ISA "can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39". The guide doesn't say anything about other ages, so I can't confirm from it how that applies to you beyond that stated range.

The documents don't cover which other options might suit you. For that, please raise it with your adviser.

The documents describe these changes from 6 April 2027:

- Under-65s can pay no more than £12,000 a tax year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance is unchanged, so the remainder can still go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already held in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own ISAs. For that, please speak to your adviser.

The £12,000 cash ISA cap applies to investors under the age of 65. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit. Money already held in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

This comes from the section "Changes from 6 April 2027" in our guide "ISAs: a guide for clients".

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, a transfer between cash ISAs should take no longer than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days. Re-registering holdings in specie can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

The new provider starts the transfer. Use their transfer process rather than withdrawing the money, so the ISA keeps its tax status. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. Money you withdraw during a tax year can be replaced in the same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The documents don't say whether this applies to ISAs held elsewhere. If you want to know what to do with your own money, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in effect. A surviving spouse or civil partner gets an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is on top of their own allowance. It applies whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

The ISA also stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. The documents don't say how this would work for your circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser.

The pension annual allowance is £60,000. This covers the total paid into your pensions in a tax year, including employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual. If you go over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due.

For high earners, the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years, provided you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

More detail is in our pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own pension. For that, an adviser would need to help.

Yes, you can still pay in, but a lower limit applies. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

The documents I have don't say how this applies to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser. More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Up to 25% of a pension can normally be taken tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above that allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't say how much you should take or when. For that, an adviser would need to help. Details are in the guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise and offer to book a free guidance appointment. We won't do this if you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

I can't tell you which option suits you. For that, an adviser would need to help.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest. The documents don't say what the rule is for transfer values of £30,000 or less.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Our pensions guide says:

- From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.
- If you die before age 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

The guide doesn't say how this applies to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser. You can read the guide at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. Our pensions guide says unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward, as long as you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

For context, the annual allowance is £60,000. For high earners it tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. I can't say how much you could carry forward or what you should do with your own pension. If you'd like that, I can pass you to an adviser.

- 0.45% a year on the portion between £1,000,000 and £3,000,000, which here is the second £1,000,000.

The annual management fee is subject to VAT. If you also have ongoing advice, both fees apply. The combined cost is set out in your client agreement and shown in pounds in your annual costs and charges statement.

More detail is on the fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Fernhill Wealth also gives independent advice. It considers products from across the whole market and isn't restricted to any provider's range.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Our discretionary investment management service is designed for portfolios of £250,000 or more. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

More details are on our fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No, there's no charge to close an account or to transfer out. On our model portfolios there are no dealing charges if holdings have to be sold. Fund charges continue to be deducted within the funds until the holdings are transferred or sold.

You can close or transfer at any time. If you'd like, your adviser can talk through your fees or performance, but you don't have to.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The funds carry their own charges. The fund managers set these, and they're deducted within the fund. The average ongoing fund charge across our model portfolios was 0.21% a year at 30 June 2026.

Each April we send every client a statement. It shows in pounds all the charges paid in the previous year, including our fees, custody, dealing and fund charges. It also shows the effect they've had on your portfolio's return. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

If you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service free of charge. The annual exempt amount for capital gains tax is £3,000. This applies to gains on investments sold in a general investment account.

Gains above that amount on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income. You can set losses against gains in the same year. You can also carry them forward if you report them to HMRC.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Dividends are tax-free within the dividend allowance of £500 a year. Above the allowance, dividends are taxed at 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers, 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers and 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers.

More detail is in our tax guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Yes. Your documents stay available in the portal for seven years after the account closes. You can request paper copies at any time at no charge.

**Discretionary management:** You agree an investment mandate and risk level with us. Our investment managers then make the day-to-day decisions within it.

**Advisory management:** We recommend changes, and you decide whether to make each one.

Which suits you depends on how involved you want to be in individual decisions. Your adviser will discuss both with you, and the choice is recorded in your suitability report. More on the service is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Where we manage your investments on a discretionary basis, the annual management fee is tiered and is subject to VAT: 0.60% a year on the first £1,000,000, 0.45% a year on the portion between £1,000,000 and £3,000,000, and 0.30% a year on the portion above £3,000,000. Fee details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Your investments are held by our independent custodian through its nominee company. Legal title is registered in the nominee's name, and you remain the beneficial owner.
